correctness.rationale: Reconstructed rank-one Schur complement: for q above both source and recipient spectral radii, qI−A of coupled graph stays positive definite iff w² D_u(q) D_v^H(q)<1; equality is linearized SIS/NIMFA threshold, not stochastic epidemic survival. In isolated clique and star blocks the connector diagonal resolvents are f=(q−r+2)/[(q+1)(q−r+1)], g=q/(q²−s), and after their unit bridge D_a=f/(1−fg), D_c=g/(1−fg). Strict block formulas show every other clique vertex is inferior to a and every leaf inferior to c, including s=1. Sign(D_a−D_c) equals sign[s(r−2)+(r−1−s)q]. For s≥r, q*=s(r−2)/(s−r+1) lies above rho(T) exactly when C_r(s)=−s²+(r²−3r+4)s−r+1>0, equivalent to r≤s<ζ_r. All other cases have unique a or c stated. Independently symbolically simplified f−g and ratio (q*²−q*−s)/C_r(s)=s/(s−r+1)², and inverted full rational 7x7 adjacency at r=s=3 q=5/2,3,4: (Da,Dc)=(78/31,70/31),(2/3,2/3),(39/118,20/59). The universal claim rests on algebraic inequalities, not these finite examples.

value.rationale: PASS: a clique weakly linked to a star is a structurally motivated competition between a dense core and a high-degree hub. The theorem gives a sharp integer leaf-count phase frontier and a genuine reversal in optimal one-contact attachment as the recovery/transmission ratio changes, not an arbitrary slice or merely a software benchmark. It is a useful exact stress test for network intervention rankings.

limitations: Symmetric weighted network, linearized homogeneous mean-field SIS threshold only.
q must exceed the spectral radii of both isolated components; an outside receiving network may mask a crossover.
No optimization of multiple bridges, stochastic extinction or nonlinear endemic prevalence.
